decision: Apply the Trøgstad fort entity point as the canonical anchor for the distributed 430-decare fort complex and retain individual fortification and public-visitor components as subanchors.
identityFindings: Trøgstad fort is a distributed inland mountain-fort complex rather than one building.
The municipality describes an approximately 430-decare site with 1.3 km of tunnels, 500 metres of trenches, two artillery batteries and outer infantry defences.
Wikidata Q19393412 and Wikimedia Commons supply a fort-complex entity point at approximately 59.63389, 11.34139.
OSM way 142710283 is a strong south-eastern fortification component but is too narrow to represent the entire complex.
chronologyFindings: The fort was constructed in 1912–1917 as part of the Fossum-sector fortifications and opened in 1917.
On 13 April 1940 it fired against German forces advancing along the road from Båstad and later toward Slitu before surrendering on 15 April.
After the war the site served as ammunition storage, radar station and school, ammunition workshop and Nike radar-control area.
The operational defensive role ended with the Nike shutdown around 1990–1991, while other military activity continued until 1995.
Indre Østfold municipality became owner in 2001 and the area now supports heritage interpretation, schools, recreation and events.

rejectedAlternatives.reason: Approximately 1.07 kilometres north-west of the documented fort core and unsupported by an object contract.
A valid fortification component but too narrow for the tunnels, batteries, infantry defences and Cold War installations across the larger site.
Useful for public visits but not the fort-complex identity.
A locality label lacks the explicit historical-entity role of Q19393412.

representationLimits: The marker represents the distributed fort complex, not one bunker or building.
The 420-metre radius covers only the central area and is not the full 430-decare site boundary.
The radius is not a tunnel, battery, property, event, closure or safety boundary.
Public outdoor routes do not imply open access to every tunnel, bunker or workshop area.
Current signs, closures, event arrangements and guided-access rules take precedence.
